o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (sakla-, “to guard, protect”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *sak (“aware, alert”). Cognate with Turkish saklamak.
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish یل (yẹl), from Proto-Turkic *yẹl.

Ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀρχαϊκός (arkhaïkós, “old-fashioned”), from ἀρχαῖος (arkhaîos, “from the beginning, antiquated, ancient, old”), from ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “beginning, origin”), from ἄρχω (árkhō, “I am first”).
From the frequentative form of Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (irde-, “to search”), from Proto-Turkic *īr-te-, from *īŕ (“trace”).
From Persian بت (“idol”), from Middle Persian bwt' (“Buddha, idol”), ultimately from Sanskrit बुद्ध (buddha).
